stem: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust. It reacts with other elements to form stable compounds, ions and molecules.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the table to give the formulae and acid/base behaviour of some of the oxides of the Period 3 elements.

| element | sodium | aluminium | silicon | phosphorus | sulfur |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| formula of oxide | $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ |  |  |  | $\text{SO}_3$ |
| acid/base behaviour |  | amphoteric |  |  |  |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Group 2 elements form stable hydroxides, with general formula $M(\text{OH})_2$, where $M$ is the Group 2 element.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Beryllium hydroxide, $\text{Be(OH)}_2$, is an amphoteric compound that shows similar chemical reactions to aluminium oxide.

State the meaning of the term *amphoteric*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write an **ionic** equation for the reaction of magnesium hydroxide, $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, with hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
(b)(iv)
parts.text: State how the solubility of the Group 2 hydroxides changes down the group.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Sodium peroxide, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$, reacts with $\text{CO}_2$.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3(\text{s}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

The partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ in a $0.500\text{ dm}^3$ sample of air is $5.37\text{ kPa}$ at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ present in the sample of air at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2(\text{s})$ that would react fully with the amount of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ calculated in **(i)**.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The peroxide ion, $\text{O}_2^{2-}$, has a single covalent bond between the two oxygen atoms. Each oxygen atom carries a negative charge.

Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram for the peroxide ion. Show outer electrons only.
